Let \(N=2q\), so \(G=R^4\) with \(R=\mathbb Z/2^N\mathbb Z\). Every additive subgroup is automatically an \(R\)-submodule.

For a subgroup \(H\), choose Smith normal form. If
\[
G/H\cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^4 \mathbb Z/2^{\alpha_i}\mathbb Z,
\qquad 0\le \alpha_1\le\cdots\le \alpha_4\le N,
\]
then after a change of basis
\[
H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^4 2^{\alpha_i}R e_i,
\]
so
\[
H\cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^4 \mathbb Z/2^{N-\alpha_i}\mathbb Z,
\]
with zero exponents omitted. Thus \(H\cong G/H\) exactly when the multiset
\[
\{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\alpha_4\}
\]
is invariant under \(\alpha\mapsto N-\alpha\).

The possible multisets are therefore:

\[
\{q,q,q,q\},
\]
\[
\{a,q,q,N-a\}\qquad 0\le a<q,
\]
\[
\{a,a,N-a,N-a\}\qquad 0\le a<q,
\]
\[
\{a,b,N-b,N-a\}\qquad 0\le a<b<q.
\]

Now count subgroups with fixed quotient type \(\alpha\). For distinct values \(\beta_1<\cdots<\beta_k\) with multiplicities \(m_1,\dots,m_k\), the number is
\[
\frac{|\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)|}
{2^{\sum_{s<t}m_sm_t}\prod_s |\mathrm{GL}_{m_s}(\mathbb F_2)|}
\cdot
2^{\sum_{s>t}m_sm_t(\beta_s-\beta_t-1)}.
\]
This comes from the orbit-stabilizer count for the canonical subgroup
\[
\bigoplus_i 2^{\alpha_i}Re_i,
\]
where the stabilizer consists of matrices whose \((i,j)\)-entry is divisible by
\[
2^{\max(0,\alpha_i-\alpha_j)}.
\]

Since
\[
|\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)|=20160,\qquad |\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_2)|=6,
\]
the four cases contribute:

\[
1,
\]
\[
\sum_{a=0}^{q-1}105\cdot 2^{6(q-a)-5},
\]
\[
\sum_{a=0}^{q-1}35\cdot 2^{8q-8a-4},
\]
\[
\sum_{0\le a<b<q}315\cdot 2^{8q-6a-2b-6}.
\]

Evaluating the geometric sums gives
\[
1+\frac{10}{3}(64^q-1)+\frac{112}{51}(256^q-1)
+\frac{28}{17}(256^q-256)-\frac{20}{3}(64^q-64).
\]
Simplifying,
\[
\boxed{\frac{196\cdot 256^q-170\cdot 64^q+25}{51}}.
\]

Thus the number of additive subgroups \(H\le G\) with \(H\cong G/H\) is

\[
\boxed{\frac{196\cdot 256^q-170\cdot 64^q+25}{51}}.
\]
